facts.text: The repository provides reinforcement learning environments for training dexterous manipulation policies with robotic hands using NVIDIA's Isaac Gym simulator
The installation instructions require downloading Isaac Gym Preview 4 from NVIDIA before the package is installed
The package pins the legacy Gym API, gym 0.23.1
DexHandBase imports isaacgym and torch at module import time
DexHandBase is the dexterous-hand environment class and extends VecTask
The custom Env base declares step, reset, render and close, each raising NotImplementedError
VecTask extends Env and parses the simulation parameters, setting dt from the configured physics timestep
The default hand asset is dexrobot_mujoco/dexrobot_mujoco/models/dexhand021_right_simplified_floating.xml
The hand has 6 base DOFs and 12 active finger DOFs
The BaseTask configuration enables policy control of the hand base (6 DOFs) and the fingers (12 controls)
The action dimension is the sum of the base DOFs and the active finger DOFs that the policy controls
The action space is a Box with low -1.0, high 1.0 and dtype float32, one element per action
The observation space is a Box from -inf to +inf with dtype float32, one element per observation
episodeLength is 300 steps
Timeout termination is raised when episode_step_count is at least episodeLength - 1
The simulation timestep is 0.005 s (200 Hz)
The default physics configuration uses 4 substeps and gravity [0.0, 0.0, -9.81]
The default position_delta scaling uses a maximum finger joint velocity of 1.0 rad/s, a maximum base linear velocity of 0.5 m/s and a maximum base angular velocity of 1.5 rad/s
The BaseTask reward has an alive term of 0.1 per step

The BaseTask policy observation lists 13 components: base positions and velocities, active finger positions and velocities, hand pose, five contact indicators, previous actions, base and finger targets, and four 35-value fingertip and fingerpad pose blocks
The observation dimension is computed at initialization from the concatenated selected components
reset resets all environments and returns the observation buffer
step applies the actions, steps physics and returns (observation, reward, done, info)
seed seeds Python's random module, numpy and torch
make_env is the main entry point for creating environments compatible with RL libraries such as rl_games
make_env loads dexhand_env/cfg/task/<task_name>.yaml when no configuration is supplied
The control timestep is measured as physics_dt times the measured number of physics steps per control step
The initial hand position is [0.0, 0.0, 0.5] and the initial hand rotation is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]

determinism.notes: the fake's reset and dynamics are deterministic, so one seed and command sequence repeat a trajectory; upstream seeds Python random, numpy and torch (vec_task.py:145-153), while the fake keeps its own seed and does not reproduce those generators

gaps: the fake is a single-environment kinematic stand-in, not Isaac Gym: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, contact forces, actuator PD control, tendon coupling or sensor noise; the five contact indicators stay zero
no rendering and no camera, video or streaming path is offered
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, so ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only

the upstream control period is measured at start-up as physics_dt times the measured physics steps per control step (physics_manager.py:243-259); the fake uses one 5 ms physics step per tick and does not reproduce that measurement
upstream step and reset return a batched (num_envs, num_observations) buffer; the bridge serves one environment, so the fake returns that row as a flat list
the fingertip and fingerpad poses are fixed hand-frame offsets in the fake; upstream derives them from the simulated hand
upstream reports the episode timeout through done without a truncated flag; the bridge exposes it as terminated
snapshot and restore are not offered: DexHandBase exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical DexHand is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step, reset and seed until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, while the last observation stays readable
